articles.title: Is Jordon Hudson at UNC game today? Updates on Bill Belichick's girlfriend in Dublin for Week 0
articles.summary: Here's updates on whether Hudson made the trip overseas.
articles.body:
As North Carolina travels to Dublin to play TCU in Week 0, Bill Belichick hopes this season is better than his first.

The Tar Heels went just 4-8 in 2025 as Belichick led the team as head coach for the first time, proving that jumping from the NFL to college is not so easy. In the process, Belichick's personal life was a huge talking point throughout the season. largely focused on his girlfriend, Jordon Hudson.

The 25-year-old immediately made her mark as Belichick relied on her to help run many areas of his career, both within the program and on the public relations side. While she has taken a step out of the spotlight more this season, the upcoming college football year could thrust her back into national news.

When the Tar Heels take the field against the Horned Frogs to open the college football season, it would not be a surprise to see Hudson on the sidelines supporting the team. Here are updates on whether Hudson made the trip overseas.

12:25 p.m. - Still no screentime yet for Hudson. Fans on X, formerly Twitter, have begun asking about her status.

12:05 p.m. - The 2026 FBS season is underway! Belichick's squad will start today's game with possession. Still no news on whether Hudson made the trip to Dublin.

11:19 a.m. - With under an hour until kickoff, the college football world is still awaiting the news of whether or not Hudson made the trip to Ireland to watch her boyfriend try and coach the Tar Heels to a surprising win over the Horned Frogs.

Kickoff will commence at around 12 p.m. ET. Stay tuned for further updates on Hudson.

Bill Belichick has been dating Jordon Hudson for several years, and the 25-year-old has become a huge part of his life. The two were first publicly together in 2024, but some reports detailed that she may have been part of his life a few years prior to that.

When Belichick was first hired by North Carolina, Hudson frequently got into hot water for seemingly being too involved in the program and Belichick's life despite not initially being on the school's payroll. Several reports from the 2025 offseason detailed how Hudson took control of Belichick's public relations appearances and was looped into many of Belichick's decisions as a head coach.

As a result, she has become a central figure in North Carolina football as long as Belichick is leading the team. Therefore, during Tar Heels' games, Hudson's appearance on the North Carolina sidelines would surely draw eyeballs.

Here's a look at when North Carolina will play during the season.

articles.title: Oregon hosting pair of 2028 top recruits for season opener
articles.summary: Oregon will host the nation's No. 2 recruit in the 2028 class, and the top in-state recruit for the season opener against Boise State.
articles.body:
The Oregon Ducks are wasting no time getting involved in the race for the top recruits in the 2028 recruiting class. Visits are already being lined up throughout the season, and the Ducks will have plenty of future talent on the sidelines for the season opener next weekend.

The Ducks locked in two more important visits for the first game of the season. Defensive lineman Kellan Hall, the No. 2 recruit in the 2028 class, and tight end Presley DeLance, the top recruit from Oregon, will both be in attendance at Autzen Stadium on Sept. 5.

Hall has already made a trip to Eugene this offseason and will be back to experience a game atmosphere against a tough opponent. The 6-foot-5, 275-pound pass rusher from Louisville, Kentucky, is a priority target for the Ducks, especially after the program missed on several defensive line targets in the 2027 class. Hall still has room to grow, and he could get bigger and stronger as a force on the interior.

Oklahoma is currently viewed as the favorite and will receive one of his 10 scheduled visits in the fall. However, Oregon has quickly built a rapport with Hall and is a key contender, alongside Kentucky, Georgia, Ohio State, Michigan, Notre Dame and more. There is still a long way to go in this recruiting process, but his athleticism as a big lineman makes him a highly coveted prospect.

The Ducks did a great job of keeping some of Oregon's top talents in-state in the 2027 cycle , landing commitments from the state's top four recruits. That effort isn't slowing down in the 2028 class, with DeLance, the top recruit in Oregon, taking a visit to Eugene.

The 6-foot-4 tight end from Lake Oswego is the No. 4 player at his position in the class, per 247Sports, after putting together a big spring and summer at different camps and landing several offers. He's quick for his size and can outrun defenders. He had a limited role as a sophomore, making just nine catches for 235 yards and a touchdown, but he is expected to see his role expand as a junior.

DeLance has scheduled eight visits for the fall and will begin his tour in the Pacific Northwest, visiting Oregon on Sept. 5 before making the trip north to visit Washington the next day. DeLance's teammate, edge rusher Josh Christensen , committed to the Ducks earlier in the offseason as part of the 2027 class, so the Ducks do have some support in the locker room.

Hall and DeLance are big targets for the Ducks, but they won't be alone on the sideline for the first game of the season. Multiple 2027 commits will be in attendance, as well as 2028 targets Jayden Bell and Tytan McNeal . It will be critical for the Ducks not only to start the season right with a victory, but to impress the next class of talent as well.

articles.title: Bournemouth 1-1 Everton: Match Report & Instant Reaction | Last gasp Tarkowski goal earns draw
articles.summary: Everton spurned a hatful of chances in the first half to go behind at Bournemouth, but captain Tarkowski equalized in time added on
articles.body:
AFC Bournemouth hosted Everton in a match that had historically favored the home side. Prior to this meeting, Bournemouth had proven to be a persistent bogey team for the Toffees, having won 9 of their 18 Premier League matchups. Everton had secured just one victory in their previous nine Premier League away games but that lone victory had come last season when the Toffees snuck a 1-0 win in December. Conversely, Bournemouth had enjoyed their own success against Everton later in the season, pulling off a disappointing 2-1 comeback victory at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium in February.

Coming into the match, Marco Rose's Bournemouth side had suffered a heartbreaking, late 2-1 defeat against Manchester City, where a Marcus Tavernier opener was cancelled out by two goals in the final six minutes. Meanwhile, after a clinical victory over Palace and then crushing Preston North End 4-0 behind a spectacular Thierno Barry hat-trick, Everton travelled to the south coast full of confidence.

The primary surprises in the lineup centered around Everton's midfield layout, where Harrison Armstrong unexpectedly started despite widespread reports in the morning suggesting he would miss the match due to advanced transfer talks with Nottingham Forest. Also, midfielder Hayden Hackney was a surprise omission from the opening eleven; having carried a minor injury knock with Moyes opting to protect him by placing him on the substitutes' bench and giving Garner another start.

The match began under cloudy skies with Everton controlling early possession and creating several dangerous opportunities. Everton were in their snazzy white away shirts with the Evertonians singing, "Don't sell Armstrong" from the kickoff.

Their best chances fell to Jarrad Branthwaite, whose glancing header was pawed away by Djordje Petrovic, and Thierno Barry, who missed a golden opportunity by firing a close-range rebound directly at the Bournemouth goalkeeper.

As the half progressed, the game grew increasingly chippy and end-to-end, testing both defenses. Jordan Pickford was forced into several sharp saves to deny dangerous breaks from Rayan and Justin Kluivert, while Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Adam Smith both picked up yellow cards for halting Everton attacks. Everton struggled with turnovers during this frantic period, allowing Bournemouth to grow into the game via sharp counterattacks.

The deadlock was finally broken just before the break when Bournemouth launched a quick counter. Evanilson held up the ball cleanly before feeding Alex Scott, who accurately picked out the far corner past a diving Pickford. As the players headed into the tunnel under a sudden torrential downpour, Everton manager David Moyes was left to ponder his tactical adjustments after a late response from Barry hit the side netting.

The second half commenced with no changes as Bournemouth kicked off, though Everton quickly pushed forward and created early attacking opportunities. Discipline became a factor as multiple players received yellow cards, and Everton had a penalty appeal turned down by VAR.

Both managers utilized their substitutes to alter the momentum of the game during the later stages. Bournemouth applied heavy pressure in the final twenty minutes, but Everton relied on desperate defending from Tarkowski and Mykolenko who made crucial blocks to stay in the match.

Everton pushed for a late breakthrough during the four minutes of added time, capitalizing on a corner kick. James Tarkowski reacted quickest to a loose ball in the box and slammed it into the far corner to secure a dramatic equalizer before the final whistle.

James Tarkowski – After struggling to cover Evanilson on the Bournemouth goal, the captain stepped up and did the job defensively to keep the match at one goal. The goal was reminiscent of his Merseyside Derby equalizer at Goodison as he drilled the ball low past Petrovic.

After the highs of Palace and Preston, the challenge of an away game against Bournemouth was a daunting one. Everton gave away the ball too frequently and struggled to deal with the Cherries counter attack. After going behind, the Blues continued to create chances and defend resolutely. Petrovic kept Everton at bay with some excellent saves and our defending kept us in the game so that the goal by Tarkowski in extra time was a fair result. The Blues also ended their streak of losing their first away game of the season at four years.

Everton applied 102 high intensity pressures in the final third against Crystal Palace last week, with only Leeds United and Manchester City making more across the first week of Premier League action. Also, no side had more shots (5) following a high turnover in the first week than the Toffees. This high intensity opening to the season was not on show today as Garner and Armstrong struggled in the middle of the park against a well organised Cherries team.

The morning news brought a shock report that claimed that Harrison Armstrong was the object of interest from Nottingham Forest. The Everton online pages were blowing up as everyone waited for the team list to be released. Thankfully, Armstrong started the match and there was a sense of relief. We have had a week of talk surrounding Ndiaye and this new report was more shocking. If TFG are considering this sale, you have to wonder what is going on at the club. Are we building or are we dismantling? The sooner this window closes the better. We have a good core to our team. Let us not throw that away.

Pickford – An alert save at the near post was impressive. Was hung out to dry on the goal. He commanded his area throughout the match.

Mykolenko – Allowed Scott too much room on the goal. A good block on the Kluivert shot prevented a goal.

Branthwaite – Solid in the middle but could have stepped up on the Scott goal.

Tarkowski – Very slow on Scott's goal but made a couple of goal saving blocks in the second half. His finish on the tying goal was quality.

Rohl – Some good tracking back to prevent a chance for Truffert. Lost possession a couple of times in dangerous places but showed tenacity to recover.

Armstrong – Struggled to get on the ball. Hopefully, he will be here next week to shine.

Garner – Looked well off the pace in the early going. Didn't track back well enough on the first Bournemouth goal.

George – His close ball control was off the charts but he faded as the game went on.

Dewsbury-Hall – Did lots of running and was the driving force going forward in the first half but lost the edge in the second half.

Ndiaye – Constantly draws players to him and his control is incredible.

Barry – Very isolated up front and should have done better when George's shot came back off the keeper.

articles.title: Carrick Rangers cruise to emphatic win over Bangor
articles.summary: Carrick Rangers cruise to a comprehensive 4-0 win over Bangor to make it three wins out of four to start the season.
articles.body:
Carrick Rangers produced a ruthless second-half display on their way to an emphatic 4-0 victory over Bangor at Clandeboye Park.

Matthew Snoddy broke the deadlock with an early strike before both Luke McCullough and Jimmy Callacher were denied by the woodwork.

Despite second-half pressure from the hosts, quickfire goals from Danny Gibson and Paul Heatley put the contest beyond reach before Joe Crowe sealed the rout with an 87th-minute stunner.

The result sees the visitors secure a third win in four league outings, while winless Bangor will be hoping to bounce back when they face the Welders in the County Antrim Shield.

The visitors got off to a dream start on seven minutes when Snoddy connected with Benjamin Buchanan-Rolleston's left-wing delivery, flicking the ball home at the front post.

That set the tone, and Stephen Baxter's side went close to doubling their advantage moments later when McCullough met Heatley's inswinging corner, only for the defender's left-footed effort from close range to cannon off the crossbar.

The chances kept coming for the away side, and on the stroke of half-time Carrick were unfortunate not to extend their lead when Callacher climbed highest to direct Heatley's curling set-piece against the woodwork.

Early in the second half, the Gers should have had their second when Mikey Place picked out Gibson with an inch-perfect cross, unmarked at the back post, and with goalkeeper Gareth Deane stranded, the striker somehow skied his effort over from point-blank range.

Gibson put that earlier miss to bed in style in the 70th minute, ghosting in behind the Bangor defence before slotting past a helpless Deane.

Heatley made sure of the points three minutes later, turning in from close range after a neat one-two with Gibson for his third league goal of the season.

A few minutes before the end, substitute Crowe added a fourth in sensational fashion, the midfielder tracking a flighted ball dropping over his shoulder before catching it sweetly on the full and rifling a blistering first-time volley past Deane.

Bangor manager Lee Feeney: "We were lucky it was only four. It was a tough one to take; I thought we were very, very naive in everything we've done. Just reflecting on it now, it could have been more, but we have to think about things and see how to approach games moving forward."

"We know what they're all about; they're the best in the league at what they do. For me, it was too easy a cross to come in and run into the blind side of our defenders, so it's everything we spoke about in the team talk not to let happen. We regrouped well and had plenty of the ball, but they just kept picking us off when we lost it."

"There was a lack of discipline and lack of experience at the back, there was no organisation, and we were leaving ourselves open, and it was just really, really disappointing."

Carrick Rangers boss Stephen Baxter: "Scoring four goals away from home without reply is always good, and we hit the woodwork numerous times as well, so that probably says a little bit about our dominance in the final third whenever we were attacking."

"Bangor had their moments and were very good in the first 20 minutes of the second half, but once we scored the second goal we started to take the game away from them."

"Paul Heatley and Danny Gibson are a lethal force when they get going, and our back three of Luke McCullough, Jimmy Callacher and BJ Burns gave us a masterclass in how to pass, play and hold a shape."

images.caption: Carrick Rangers cruise to emphatic win over Bangor

articles.title: New York Yankees vs. Boston Red Sox: Carlos Rodón vs. Jake Bennett
articles.summary: The Yankees play two today. Let’s start it with a bang?
articles.body:
A 1-0 win is as nailbiting as it gets, but it's still a win. The Yankees took the first round of this big four-game series last night, setting them up well for a good weekend. Hopefully they can do it in a less-stressful way, with two games against the Red Sox today and sending lefties to the hill in both of them.

Carlos Rodón does get the ball for the day half of today's doubleheader, signaling a grumpy day for me. He's on a three-win pace if he had been healthy all year, which is more than enough given he's the fourth option in the rotation, but the aesthetic experience of him is far worse than the analytical. He's only gone four innings his last two starts, despite allowing a single earned run in both, because his control has been rather spotty since coming off the IL (and he's had a pitch count to consider). On a day where we'll play two, let's hope he figures out a bit of length and saves a bullpen that may be needed with Max Fried coming off the injured list himself. Rodón threw 76 pitches in his last outing, so that's the baseline.

Before opening FanGraphs, I could have sworn Jake Bennett was an MLB: The Show create-a-player, but the 6-foot-6 lefty does seem to be a real person. Boston seems to run this pattern of large lefties who don't strike many people out but somehow never give up home runs, and Bennett follows this archetype. I regret to inform Yankee fans we may see some repeats of last night given Bennett's talents and the apparent inability of the Yankees to elevate contact against southpaws, but I also reserve the right to be surprised.

There are a couple changes to the lineup from last night, with Spencer Jones taking over in center field, Ali Sánchez behind the plate, and Amed Rosario starting at third and also batting third. I'm not sure any of those moves are necessarily upgrades from what the team had on Friday, but if they score more than one run it's all gravy.

Rejoice for this game is back on normal channels.

articles.title: 4 fantasy football targets worth investing blind confidence in
articles.summary: These unproven players could lead you to fantasy football glory
articles.body:
Fantasy football drafts aren't won in Round 1. It's the picks you make later that define your team, along with the savvy waiver wire pickups you make along the way.

That means deviating from ADP in drafts, which is easier said than done. Nobody wants to be the person whose picks are mocked by their friends. It's a lot more fun to have a roster worth flaunting about, like Patrick Bateman flashing his business card to his highfalutin buddies in American Psycho .

Winning the draft, however, pales in comparison to winning a championship. So, have some gumption about your guys, even if it means taking them well before they were slated to go. And even if they haven't exactly proved worthy of their draft position yet.

We're highlighting four players who fit that second category, so here's a look at a group worth being blindly confident about in drafts.

Burden was incredible in limited snaps for Chicago last season, plus with DJ Moore and Olamide Zaccheaus gone, he's slated to be a full-time starting WR in Ben Johnson's explosive offense. While Burden is going as early as the fourth round despite a lack of production and a training camp groin injury, he has the talent to be a top-10 player at the position.

Fantasy football managers may be wary of rookie running backs after Ashton Jeanty and Omarion Hampton underwhelmed last season. Price, though, is worth taking another swing, as he very well could be the leading rusher for the reigning Super Bowl champions. Zach Charbonnet is coming off a torn ACLa and Kenneth Walker is on the Kansas City Chiefs, while Seattle invested a first-round pick in Price and clearly believes in him.

Kyle Shanahan has been known to make rookies work their way onto the field gradually, but Stribling's dominance in camp -- combined with injuries to Mike Evans and Ricky Pearsall, the latter of which is season-ending -- won't allow him to wait. Stribling has a chance to be San Francisco's top pass-catcher from Day 1, as he offers a strong 6-foot-2 frame and plenty of athletic ability after the catch.

A blazing fast running back who sat behind Travis Etienne Jr. last season, Tuten is expected to be the lead ball-carrier now, and Liam Coen could turn him into a fantasy football superstar. Chris Rodriguez could potentially steal goal line carries, but Tuten's immense athletic ability will make him difficult to take off the field in any situation. He's going much higher in drafts than his rookie year production would suggest, and he's worth the gamble.

articles.title: Darius Slayton could be out with the Giants
articles.summary: With so much focus on whether former Giants star receiver Odell Beckham Jr. will make the team in his first year back on the roster since 2018, a receiver dr...
articles.body:
With so much focus on whether former Giants star receiver Odell Beckham Jr. will make the team in his first year back on the roster since 2018, a receiver drafted a month after OBJ would traded is in danger of not surviving Sunday's cuts.

Paul Schwartz of the New York Post reports that Darius Slayton is on the bubble .

The report is bolstered by specific facts. First, Schwartz writes that Slayton is "clearly not moving the same" after surgery to repair a sports hernia. Second, Slayton played extensively in the preseason finale against the Jets — a game during which most of the obvious starters were held out.

Slayton stayed in the game even after quarterback Jameis Winston exited for Brandon Allen.

Slayton and Beckham, who possibly are competing for the same spot on the 53-man roster, played 33 snaps each. (Isaiah Hodgins and Dalen Cambre had 37 snaps each.)

A fifth-round pick in 2019, Slayton has appeared in 106 regular-season games with 78 starts in seven seasons. Last year, he signed a three-year, $36 million contract.

He's due to make $12.25 million in salary this year, with $500,000 in per-game active roster bonuses. A whopping $9.75 million of his salary is fully guaranteed.

Cutting him would leave behind a $12.75 million cap charge in 2026, with another $3 million applying in 2027.

A trade is also possible, in theory. The Giants surely would have to pay a significant portion of his guaranteed salary in order to make it happen.

The team's preseason depth chart continues to list Slayton as a starter, along with Malik Nabers.

articles.title: Dave Roberts reacts to concerning Shohei Ohtani development before Tigers game
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts gave an update superstar Shohei Ohtani's pitching status.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are 81-54 on the precipice of September, first place in the National League West and nine games up on the second-place San Diego Padres. They are in possession of the NL's No. 2 seed.

The Dodgers have done a lot of this winning despite some major injuries to their starting pitching staff. High-paid arms like Tyler Glasnow and Blake Snell have missed significant time, but did recently rejoin the staff.

Superstar two-way player Shohei Ohtani started the season on the mound, managing to stay healthy for the first half of the schedule. However, his last start came on July 3 and he has been out with injury since.

Apr 15, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers two-way player Shohei Ohtani pitches against the New York Mets in the first inning at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The 32-year-old was supposed to make a start right before the All-Star break, but was scratched because of bicep and knee problems. Almost two months later, it has been left knee inflammation that has kept him off the mound.

Ohtani made 14 starts before injury, spinning 85 ⅔ innings. He is 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA, striking out 95 and walking 26. It was shaping up to be the best pitching season of his illustrious career.

He has not pitched in almost two months now, but it was reported earlier this week that Ohtani might return to the mound on Sunday at the Detroit Tigers. That hope has now been dashed by manager Dave Roberts' recent comments.

The fact that Ohtani might have got back in there Aug. 30 does suggest that he will pitch in September. At that, he should have enough time to build up for the postseason.

During this, the six-time All-Star has still been hitting. In 196 plate appearances since his last pitching appearance, he is slashing .274/.347/.560 (.907 OPS) with 12 home runs and 30 RBIs.

Those are of course elite numbers, but might leave something to be desired seeing as it is Ohtani. Perhaps this knee injury may be affecting him slightly on the hitting side. Even if he does not pitch Sunday, there is plenty of time for a ramp-up before the playoffs begin.

articles.title: North Dakota State Dominated FCS. Does That Predict Success In FBS?
articles.summary: North Dakota State and Sacramento State make the jump from FCS to FBS in 2026. Historical data shows which traits best predict immediate competitiveness at t...
articles.body:
Two programs make their FBS debuts today, and the betting market has very different expectations for them. North Dakota State opens its first FBS season at home against Jacksonville State. Despite being the newcomer, NDSU is a 6.5-point favorite. Sacramento State, which also moves up from FCS this year, opens at Eastern Michigan as a 9.5-point underdog.

That is a 17-point difference between two programs making the same formal jump in competition. Their recent histories in FCS competition help explain why. North Dakota State has spent more than a decade as the standard in FCS football. The Bison finished their 22-year FCS tenure with a 50-5 record in the playoffs , including 10 national championships. They went 12-1 last season before beginning the move to FBS. Sacramento State has also had strong seasons, including a 12-1 run to the FCS quarterfinals in 2022, but its recent results have been less consistent.

Both programs officially begin FBS competition in 2026 . North Dakota State joins the Mountain West as a football-only member, while Sacramento State joins the MAC. The question is whether their FCS records tell us much about what comes next.

How Five Year FCS Success Translates To First Year FBS Performance

To examine whether success at the FCS level carries over immediately to FBS, I first looked at established FCS programs that moved up since 2012 and had at least five seasons of history before playing their first full FBS schedule. Startup programs such as UTSA, Georgia State and Charlotte were excluded because they did not have five comparable FCS seasons.

For each program, I calculated its record over the five seasons immediately preceding its first full FBS season, then compared it with its record during Year 1 in FBS. The NCAA's realignment history confirms the recent additions to the group, including James Madison, Jacksonville State, Sam Houston, Kennesaw State, Delaware and Missouri State, followed by North Dakota State and Sacramento State in 2026.

In practical terms, teams that won more in FCS have done slightly better after moving up, on average. Their FCS record alone provides little certainty about how their first FBS season will unfold. The individual programs make that clear. James Madison had won 84.8% of its games over the five seasons before moving to FBS in 2022. The Dukes immediately went 8-3 and finished atop the Sun Belt East in their first season. Georgia Southern and Jacksonville State also transitioned well. Georgia Southern went 9-3 in its first FBS season, while Jacksonville State finished 9-4 in 2023.

Other successful FCS programs had a much harder time. Coastal Carolina had won 77.3% of its games during the five-year period before its first FBS season. The Chanticleers went 3-9 in 2017. Sam Houston presents an even stronger counterexample. The Bearkats had won more than 72% of their games during the five-year window and captured an FCS national championship before moving up. They finished 3-9 in their first full FBS season in 2023. Sam Houston's move also followed an unusual transition period that included the shortened spring 2021 season and a nine-game 2022 schedule.

A simple linear regression confirms the lack of strong predictive power. Five-year performance has a positive relationship with first-year FBS performance, but a weak one. Five-year winning percentage explains only about 5.4% of the variation in first-year FBS winning percentage, with a correlation of 0.23. The regression would place NDSU at roughly a .550 first-year FBS winning percentage and Sacramento State around .440 based on five-year record alone. Given how little variation the model explains, those numbers are better viewed as historical benchmarks than forecasts. Saturday will provide the first data point for both.

Predicting FBS Success From FCS Winning Percentage

A closer look at the historical transitions produced a much stronger signal than the five-year winning percentage alone. Two variables stood out:

Winning percentage in the program's final FCS season

Whether the program reached at least the FCS semifinals during the previous five seasons

A regression using those two factors explains 37.4% of the variation in first-year FBS winning percentage across the historical sample. The model estimates that every additional 10 percentage points of winning percentage in a team's final FCS season is associated with about 5.2 additional percentage points of first-year FBS winning percentage. Reaching at least an FCS semifinal during the preceding five years adds another 16.7 percentage points, holding final-season performance constant.

That model paints a particularly favorable picture for North Dakota State. The Bison finished their final FCS season 12-1, a .923 winning percentage, and easily satisfy the deep-playoff criterion after multiple championship and semifinal appearances over the previous five seasons. The model estimates a 71.6% first-year FBS winning percentage, equivalent to about 8.6 wins over a 12-game schedule.

Sacramento State enters with a different profile. The Hornets finished 2025 at 7-5, a .583 winning percentage, and did not reach an FCS semifinal during the five-year window. Their deepest postseason run was a quarterfinal appearance in 2022. The model estimates a 37.3% first-year FBS winning percentage, equivalent to about 4.5 wins.

The striking part is how closely those estimates line up with the betting market. Current season win totals list North Dakota State at 8.5 wins and Sacramento State at 4.5. A model built entirely from the recent FCS performance of previous programs making the jump arrives at essentially the same numbers. That agreement does not make the regression a substitute for the much broader information incorporated into betting markets. It does suggest that a program's performance immediately before moving up, combined with evidence of recent postseason success, captures a meaningful amount of its readiness to compete at the FBS level.

What FBS Conferences Should Look For In FCS Expansion Candidates

For FBS conferences evaluating potential new members, the key question may be which programs are positioned to compete at a high level immediately. In this small historical sample, the strongest signals were recent winning performance and deep FCS playoff success. North Dakota State checks both boxes, while Sacramento State enters with a more modest profile.
